QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_22

question.text: A portfolio has a value of Rs. 200 crore and a modified duration of 4 years. Bond futures with a duration of 8 years are priced at Rs. 2,00,000 per contract. To increase portfolio duration to 6 years, how many contracts should be bought?

explanation.text: The Logic: Applying the duration-gap form of the duration-based hedge ratio (workbook pp. 164-165): Contracts = Portfolio value x (Target duration - Current duration) / (Per-contract futures value x Futures duration) = 200,00,00,000 x (6 - 4) / (2,00,000 x 8) = 2,500. Positive sign = buy. The Trap: 5,000 uses the target duration alone. 1,250 uses the current duration alone. 10,000 ignores the futures duration. Note: Buying GOI bond futures increases portfolio duration; selling them reduces it (workbook p. 187).
